a0_question: One of these marks is a scratch. The other is just a reflection. Can you tell which one you would pay for?
a1_bill: One Hertz renter got a four hundred and forty dollar bill for a one-inch scuff, minutes after returning the car. A House subcommittee chair says Hertz bills from these scans without human review. The company has an AI scanner. The renter has a phone.
a2_idea: Twice gives the renter proof. Take the same photo twice: when you move in, and when you move out.
a3_guide: At move-out, a ghost of your first photo walks you back to the exact spot. The shutter fires when OpenCV locks on.
a4_car: So: scratch, or reflection? One photo cannot tell. Twice asks for one more, from a step to the side. The reflection slides away. The scratch stays put.
a5_room: In the living room, the new shadow is ruled out. The stain and the scuff stay.
a6_report: Every finding lands in a signed report. The move-in photos were sealed before the move-out photos existed.
a7_verify: Anyone can check it, without trusting us. Change one byte, and the check fails.
a8_cloud: OpenCV 5 does the vision, on AWS. Object detection runs on the new DNN engine, more than three times faster than the classic one.
a9_numbers: On our benchmark, Twice finds eighty-eight percent of the damage, and every flag is real. On twenty-two real photo pairs of unchanged scenes: zero false alarms.
a10_close: Your next move-out starts with today's photos. Take them twice.
